To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the application of HLS techniques to the design of microprocessor functional blocks can potentially lead to faster design space exploration, and that the use of HLS in such a context is not as simple as it is for general purpose applications.
(1) the HLS techniques are applicable for the design of microprocessor functional blocks and (2) the use of HLS can potentially speed up microprocessor design by a factor of 2 to 3.

• HLS can be applied to a large number of microprocessor functional blocks, • HLS can be used to design these blocks, and • HLS can be a useful technique for the design of microprocessor functional block designs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
application of HLS to a new domain of microprocessor design and is aimed at enabling efficient exploration of design space for high-performance microprocessor designs.
the application of HLS to a domain that is not well served by it and is a step in the direction of making HLS a viable design methodology in the design of high performance microprocessors.

the following: (1) identifying and formulating a methodology for application of classical high-level synthesis to a new domain, (2) developing a set of source-level compiler optimizations that enable efficient chaining of operations in a functional block and (3) applying high-level synthesis techniques for efficient synthesis of high-performance microprocessor functional blocks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methodology proposed in this paper is an important step in the direction of applying HLS to the microprocessor domain.
our methodology enables efficient chaining of the operations and high-level transformations of the functional blocks that are essential for the microprocessor designs.
our methodology is a step towards the application of HLS in microprocessor design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to show that HLS can be applied to a microprocessor design domain that is very different from the classical HLS domains of DSP and image processing.
we have developed a methodology that enables high-level synthesis of functional blocks of high performance microprocessors and demonstrated it on a Pentium®-like decoder design.
we have demonstrated a methodology for the use of HLS for microprocessor designs that can potentially speedup the design space exploration of these complex blocks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HLS techniques can be applied to a domain that has been traditionally considered too complex and thus not amenable to HLS.
HLS is a powerful and efficient tool to design and implement complex microprocessor functional blocks.
high-level synthesis can be applied to microprocessor design, but the methodology must be tailored for the specific domain.
